name: John Curtis

issue_poll.name: Deseret News/Hinckley Institute poll (Dan Jones & Associates), Sept 3–21, 2024
issue_poll.note: Most important issue when choosing a senator; health care, education and environment tied at 9% ('other' dropped). Poll listed only nine testable issues, so Housing (No. 1 in Utah Foundation's 2024 Utah Priorities Project, Feb–Mar 2024) added as rank 10.

issues.position: Extend the 2017 tax cuts; no tax increases

issues.issue: Role of the federal government / public lands
issues.position: Shift federal land to state control; limit monument designations
issues.note: No floor vote on land transfer or monument limits; Grand Staircase CRA expired without a vote.

issues.position: Tie federal college funding to graduates' outcomes
issues.note: H.R.1 cut loan access for programs whose graduates earn too little.

issues.position: Tariff on Chinese imports based on pollution
issues.note: No floor vote on a pollution-based tariff this term.

issues.position: Pro-life; leave abortion law to the states
issues.note: No floor vote on a federal abortion ban or protection this term.

issues.position: Pass H.R.2; fund border; reimburse states aiding border
issues.note: H.R.1 funded border enforcement and a $13.5B state border reimbursement fund.
No floor vote on Supreme Court term limits this term.

issues.position: Sell some BLM land to localities for housing (HOUSES Act)
issues.note: Land-sale provision dropped from H.R.1 before the vote; no standalone floor vote.

caveats: Rank 10 (Housing) comes from a different Utah poll because the closest poll listed only nine testable issues.
S.6 Born-Alive cloture (Jan 22, 2025; Curtis Yea) not counted for Abortion: it covers care after birth, not state vs federal abortion law.
Campaign site (johncurtis.org) could not be fetched; positions come from news coverage, debate reports and his own op-ed.
Three of three recorded votes are the single H.R.1 package, counted once per issue it touched.
